replication.target_description: participants; predictors versus experiencers, paintings; authors’ post-replication report focal test.

n.exclusions: Preregistered eligibility, completion and attention checks; see report Sample and protocol deviations.
n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, the average number of paintings Predictors (n = 106) believe they would need to see to reach a verdict was 15.575 (sd = 11.497), while Experiencers (n = 108) needed to see 3.759 (sd = 3.793) to reach a verdict. This difference of 11.816 (se = 1.166) was tested using an independent samples t-test with equal variances (t(212) = 10.134, p < 0.0001; n = 214). As a result, we can reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the number of paintings Predictors believe they would need to see to reach a verdict and the number of paintings Experiencers need to see to reach a verdict. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 1.386 (95% CI [1.116, 1.655]).
